title: Diff-MoE: Efficient Batched MoE Inference with Priority-Driven Differential Expert Caching
problem: MoE models require massive expert parameter storage; existing GPU memory management solutions use sophisticated prefetching but suffer communication bottlenecks at large batch sizes
motivation: MoE inference is bandwidth-limited on GPUs; enabling efficient multi-batch inference could unlock higher throughput for LLM serving with resource constraints
method: The approach uses a priority-ranked cache system to manage where different experts are stored based on usage patterns. Experts that are used frequently across the entire model stay in high-priority caches at each layer, where they're fastest to access. Experts used frequently within specific layers sit in medium-priority caches managed by least-recently-used (LRU) replacement—a strategy that removes the oldest unused item when space is needed—combined with predictive prefetching (loading experts before they're requested, based on patterns). The least frequently-used experts are loaded into cache only when needed, on-demand.
key_novelty: The key innovation is organizing expert caches into different priority levels based on both overall popularity and recent usage—the first approach to jointly optimize for both global and temporal patterns in MoE inference.
contributions: Identification of global and temporal locality in expert activation patterns
Lightweight predictor for prefetching next-layer experts
2.74x throughput improvement vs DeepSpeed, 2.22x vs Pre-gated MoE, 1.55x vs MoE-Infinity
limitations: Limited to MoE architectures; predictor accuracy not quantified; assumes structured expert activation patterns; evaluation on specific GPU types
